docsArticles.displayName: Sign in and create your account
docsArticles.title: Sign in and create your account
docsArticles.excerpt: How to sign in, create or manage your account, accept a team invite, and recover access without sharing passwords or codes.
docsArticles.bodyMarkdown:
# Sign in and create your account

Use this site's account pages to sign in, create an account, manage your profile, or recover access. We never ask you to share your password, one-time codes, or recovery codes with support staff.

## Sign in

Open the sign in page, enter your email and password, then choose Sign in. If you have multi-factor authentication or a passkey set up, you will be prompted to complete it.

## Create an account

Choose Create account from the sign in page. Use an email address you can receive messages at, and choose a password you do not use anywhere else. You may be asked to verify your email before you can sign in.

## Forgot your password

Choose Forgot password from the sign in page. We will email a reset link to the address on your account. The link expires after a short time so your account stays safe even if your inbox is ever exposed.

## Manage your profile and account

After signing in, open /profile to change your display name, profile image, contact details, sign-in methods, and security settings. The profile workspace keeps account details private to the signed-in user.

If you signed up with email, you can also link a sign-in provider such as Google or Apple from your account workspace, so you can choose how to sign in next time. You can unlink a provider whenever you like, as long as you keep at least one other way to sign in.

## Accept a team invite

If someone has invited you to an organization, you will get an email with a link to accept the invite. Open the link and either sign in to an existing account or create a new one. After you accept, you will be added to the organization with the role the inviter chose.

If the link no longer works, ask the person who invited you to send a new invite. Invite links expire for safety. Do not forward your invite link to anyone else, even people on the same team.

## Get help with account access

If you cannot sign in or did not receive an expected email, use the account support form. Never share your password, recovery codes, or one-time sign-in codes with anyone, including site support.

docsArticles.title: Keep your account secure
docsArticles.excerpt: Verify your email, troubleshoot sign-in links, turn on multi-factor authentication or a passkey, and recover access safely.
docsArticles.bodyMarkdown:
# Keep your account secure

A few simple steps make it much harder for someone else to access your account.

## Email verification and sign-in links

We send verification, reset, and sign-in links to the email address on your account. Verifying your email proves you control it and lets us send you password resets and security notices. Open the verification email and follow the link.

Sign-in and verification links expire after a short time so your account stays safe even if your inbox is ever exposed.

- If you did not get the email, check your spam or junk folder and confirm you used the right address. Then return to the sign in or create-account page and request a new email.
- If the link no longer works, request a fresh one from the sign in page. Old links stop working once you request a new one or once you have already used them.
- If you sign in with an instant link instead of a password, open the link on the same device when possible, and never forward sign-in links to anyone else.

## Use a strong, unique password

Choose a password you do not use on any other site. A password manager can generate and remember one for you. Change your password right away if you think anyone else has seen it.

## Turn on multi-factor authentication or a passkey

In your /profile security settings, turn on multi-factor authentication or register a passkey. With either one on, signing in requires both your password and your device or authenticator app, so a stolen password is not enough.

## Review your active sessions

The /profile workspace lists devices that are currently signed in. If you see one you do not recognize, sign it out and change your password.

## Recover your account safely

If you lose access, use the forgot password or instant link options on the sign in page. We will never ask you to share your password, multi-factor codes, recovery codes, or session tokens with support staff. Treat any such request as a phishing attempt.
